audit.whatIsWrong: Eight strings say Null Sphere silences: early ('his Q silence ... the silence plus his passive magic shield'), mid ('Q-silence me'), whys[2] ('His Q silence ... no way to all-in through the silence'), whys[3] ('any commit you make eats the silence'), whys[4] ('the Q-silence burst'), spikes[1].text ('Q silence plus passive shield'), wants.foe[1] ('shielded Q-silence burst rotation') and wants.foe[2] ('poke with Q silence').
audit.why: Null Sphere has not silenced since V4.4 — the patch history reads 'No longer silences, but will still interrupt channels and charges'. Riot's current text is 'deals damage and interrupts channels. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' The advice built on the silence is actively wrong: the entry tells the player he cannot all-in through the silence, when in fact nothing stops his Q, W, E or R after being hit by it. What actually blunts the all-in is the shield, which is a different problem with a different answer.
audit.corrected: All eight rewritten around Null Sphere's channel interrupt and its shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: The shield is repeatedly credited to his passive — 'passive magic shield', 'passive shield', 'through his passive shield'.
audit.why: Void Stone is not a shield. It is flat magic damage reduction plus ignoring unit collision. The absorb shield comes off Null Sphere itself. The distinction matters twice over: the shield is spent and can be baited, while Void Stone is permanent and cannot, and Void Stone is quietly reducing Spirit Fire and Fury of the Sands — Nasus's only two sources of area damage, both magic — every second of the lane. That is a permanent tax on his kit the entry never mentions.
audit.corrected: Shield attributed to Null Sphere; Void Stone's magic reduction stated in dontsFull, phases[5] and the mid text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse is never mentioned, and nothing warns that Nasus's own casts feed it.
audit.why: Force Pulse's cooldown drops by 0.75 seconds every time Kassadin or a nearby champion casts an ability. A Nasus dropping Spirit Fire on the wave beside him is charging the enemy's cone for him. That is genuinely counter-intuitive tech — it is the only case in this matchup where playing the lane normally hands the opponent a cooldown — and it is cheap to avoid once you know.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone's unit-collision clause is never used.
audit.why: Kassadin ignores unit collision, so the standard melee trick of putting the minion wave between yourself and a walk-up does not work on him. For a champion whose whole early game is 'farm behind the wave and do not get reached', that is worth knowing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rated FAVOURED, difficulty 4/10, on a lane Nasus loses at 47.63% over 443 games, and whose own chart gives Kassadin four of seven stages.
audit.why: The entry's own prose says 'Once Kassadin hits 6 the lane is his' and 'His first-item spike is the scariest stretch'. FAVOURED 4/10 is the field a player reads before any of that and it points the wrong way.
audit.corrected: diffRating 7/10, breakdown.difficulty and the final rating line corrected. diff itself must go FAVOURED to HARD by hand — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4] 'Level 6' reads 'First real fight you're allowed to take' and phases[5] 'First item' sells the Sheen spike — while the content layer says level 6 is where the lane becomes his and his first AP item is his real spike.
audit.why: Level 6 is when Riftwalk arrives. Telling a Nasus that this is his first sanctioned fight is the exact opposite of the truth and is the kind of line that loses a lane. The two layers give opposite instructions for both stages.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and phases[5].why rewritten to match reality. phases[1].side set to Nasus to match content win[1]; the remaining side mismatches are blocked — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and whys[4] both call Fury of the Sands a 'single-target ult'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'unleashes a mighty sandstorm that batters nearby enemies ... damages nearby enemies'. It is an aura. The point the sentences are reaching for — that it does nothing to a target who has already blinked away — is true, but it is about him leaving, not about the ult being single-target.
suspectNames flagged 'Farm Siphoning Strike' in wants.you[0]. False positive — Siphoning Strike is the real Q name; 'Farm' is the sentence's verb. No edit made.

edits.after: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Riftwalk and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — 5s at rank 1 falling to 2s, so it is never truly down. Wither the blink in, not the exit.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips dives: pop R, Wither Kassadin, and suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.
edits.after: Riftwalk arrives and the lane turns his: he blinks in, bursts and leaves before the slow can land. Hold R and Wither for a commit, never a chase.

edits.after: His first AP item is the real spike here, not your Sheen — and Void Stone quietly cuts the magic damage of Spirit Fire and your ult.

edits.before: That is Kassadin's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Void Stone reduces magic damage, so Spirit Fire and your ult both land lighter on him.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: He ignores unit collision, so minions will never body-block his walk-up.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a non-event in my favor only because Kassadin is even weaker than I am pre-6 and has to walk into melee range to farm. I just soak Siphoning Strike stacks off the wave and accept that I cannot punish him hard yet. At 3 Wither flips a clean window: if he steps up to last-hit I can land the attack-speed plus movement slow, walk him down with autos, and chunk him while he has no Riftwalk to escape. Do not overcommit into his Q silence though, because the silence plus his passive magic shield turns a greedy all-in into a feed.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a non-event in my favor only because Kassadin is even weaker than I am pre-6 and has to walk into melee range to farm. I just soak Siphoning Strike stacks off the wave and accept that I cannot punish him hard yet. At 3 Wither flips a clean window: if he steps up to last-hit I can land the attack-speed plus movement slow, walk him down with autos, and chunk him while he has no Riftwalk to escape. Null Sphere does not silence — it interrupts channels — but it leaves him a magic shield, so a greedy all-in still bleeds out on it.

edits.before: Once Kassadin hits 6 the lane is his. Riftwalk lets him blink in, Q-silence me through his passive shield, burst, and blink back out before my Wither slow or Spirit Fire DoT can do anything to a target that is already gone. I cannot chase a champion who escapes on a low-cooldown blink, and my single-target ult does nothing if he never stands still. So levels 4-6 I stop trying to win and just farm stacks, hold Wither for when he actually commits onto me, and play not to die. Ping for ganks constantly, because Wither into a jungler is the one way I punish his short Riftwalk.
edits.after: Once Kassadin hits 6 the lane is his. Riftwalk lets him blink in, land Null Sphere and the shield it gives him, burst, and blink back out before my Wither slow or Spirit Fire can touch a target that is already gone. I cannot chase a champion escaping on a 5-second blink that falls toward 2, and Void Stone blunts the magic damage of both my E and my ult on top. So levels 4-6 I stop trying to win and just farm stacks, hold Wither for when he actually commits onto me, and play not to die. Ping for ganks — Wither into a jungler is the one way I punish a short Riftwalk.

edits.before: His first-item spike is the scariest stretch, but the late game swings back to me hard if I survived it. By two-plus items my Siphoning Strike is fat, Fury of the Sands gives me the bonus HP and per-second magic damage to tank his burst, and a maxed Wither shuts off his blink-kite long enough to land an empowered Q. The whole fight hinges on Wither: catch his Riftwalk-in with the slow and a squishy Kassadin cannot kite my stacked Q and ult, and he folds. Miss it and he blinks out and resets. Build some MR and a component to eat his shielded burst, and look to splitpush where my Q-stacking and duel power matter more than his pick potential.
edits.after: His first-item spike is the scariest stretch, but the late game swings back to me hard if I survived it. By two-plus items my Siphoning Strike is fat, Fury of the Sands gives me the bonus HP to tank his burst, and a maxed Wither shuts off his blink-kite long enough to land an empowered Q. The whole fight hinges on Wither: catch his Riftwalk-in with the slow and a squishy Kassadin cannot kite my stacked Q, and he folds. Miss it and he resets. Build MR to eat the burst, and note that Force Pulse charges off nearby spellcasts — my own Spirit Fire hands him his cone, so do not spam it beside him.

edits.before: His Q silence plus passive magic shield lets him win the level-3 poke trade your Spirit Fire cannot answer, and you have no way to all-in through the silence.
edits.after: Null Sphere shields him as it damages you, so he wins the level-3 poke trade, and Void Stone blunts the Spirit Fire chip you would answer it with.

edits.after: He hoards levels and pokes with a shielded Null Sphere while you are stuck farming, and any commit you make eats a free burst rotation.

edits.after: Riftwalk unlocks his entire kit — he blinks in for the Null Sphere burst and blinks out before your Wither slow or Fury of the Sands can put a mark on him.
